text:
incident-bot: ALERT: paged-kv-cache.eviction_rate > 0.8 on prod-us-west-2. Instances r-infer-*-pool-3 reporting sustained GC and increased latency. Pager: eng-runtime oncall.

alex: @incident-bot ack — I'm looking. p95 token latency jumping from ~80ms to ~420ms across generation routes.

maria: sending logs? any obvious OOMs? :eyes:

alex: dumping recent logs now. seeing repeated lines like `evict_block: id=0x7f.. size=65536 policy=LRU` every few ms, and an odd ramp in metadata entries per key. counts: before 02:00 UTC ~12, now ~320. not typical.

samir: that smells like metadata leak in block-manager, or the block size tuning interacting badly with the new continuous-batching release we rolled at 01:05. continuous-batching v2 raised max_batch_size to 4096; could be increasing resident KV handles.

lina: @alex can you check which pools are hot? I can start a config hotfix if we confirm.

alex: hot pools: gen-v2-pool-3, chat-serve-pool-1. memory at 93% on those. evictions are thrashing, I can reproduce locally with a reduced trace.

kevin: we have two levers: 1) throttle batching (quick) 2) adjust block-manager eviction/window parameters (safer but needs deploy). I'd do 1 first to buy time.

alex: agree. I'm going to roll back the continuous-batching override for the affected routing tag to max_batch_size=1024 and reduce batch_hold_ms to 4ms. Doing a canary change on gen-v2-pool-3 now.

alex: (exec)
```
# temp change via runtime-config API
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/configs/patch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route_tag":"gen-v2-pool-3","continuous_batching":{"max_batch_size":1024,"batch_hold_ms":4}}'
```

ops-bot: deploy started by alex. canary target: gen-v2-pool-3.

maria: watching metrics. evictions per second dropped ~60% on the canary within 45s. p95 down to ~120ms. great.

samir: good. while that's stabilizing, I'll prepare a post-deploy patch to address the metadata leak in the block manager. hypothesis: reference count growth when blocks split under large batches; small chimney where metadata pointers aren't reclaimed until later.

lina: can we also tune block_size? current config uses 64KB blocks (64*1024). if we reduce to 32KB blocks we may reduce peak resident set but increase metadata entries slightly. tradeoff.

alex: can we metricize that trade quickly? we need low-latency customers to not see 5xx.

kevin: customer impact: early signal shows ~12 customers experienced transient 502s on generation endpoints, primarily those routed to gen-v2-pool-3. CS reported two enterprise customers — RJ-498 and OakTree Analytics — saw request timeouts and error spikes.

maria: I'm drafting a short incident note for CS: include TL;DR, mitigation (batching rollback), ETA for full fix (3-5 hours), and affected routes.

alex: can we also enable prefix KV caching bypass for embeddings routes? that should reduce cache pressure for embedding-heavy keys. I'll flip a feature flag on the pool: `kv_prefix_bypass=true` for embeddings.

alex: (exec)
```
# enable prefix bypass on chat-serve-pool-1
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/configs/patch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route_tag":"chat-serve-pool-1","kv":{"prefix_bypass":true}}'
```

ops-bot: flag change applied on chat-serve-pool-1.

maria: metrics show memory stabilizing across the two hot pools after both changes. evictions subsided, p99 latency improving. I'll notify CS with a short note and list of impacted customers + RCA pending.

samir: for the full fix I'm opening a PR to address the block-manager metadata leak. plan: 1) add stricter refcount decrements when blocks are split/merged, 2) add a GC pass that runs on low-load windows to reclaim orphaned meta entries, 3) add unit tests to simulate high-split churn. target deploy: next minor release in ~48h unless urgent backport needed.

lina: additionally we should evaluate tuned block_size for gen workloads. propose experiment: prod canary of 32KB block size on a single pool for 6 hours, compare RSS and metadata counts. I'll own that if ops approves.

kevin: ops approved. schedule the canary window in 30m after this thread.

alex: quick note on customer impact assessment: total error rate spike ~0.9% across generation requests during the peak; two customers had >5% errors for 10–12 minutes. we've opened INC-2026-342 for customer-facing tracking and RJ ticket RJ-789 for engineering follow-up.

maria: handoff to next oncall @samir for follow-up and monitoring tonight. I'll keep CS notified and post a summary to #incidents once we have the initial RCA.

samir: taking handoff. monitoring dashboards set to alert on eviction_rate>0.2 now. leaving notes: revert continuous-batching rollback only when eviction_rate < 0.05 for 30m and p99 < 200ms.

alex: logs attached in the incident channel gist: https://internal.gists/abcd1234 — includes sample eviction stacks and metadata counts.

maria: nice work team. post-incident checklist: 1) customer comms (CS) 2) patch PR for metadata leak 3) block_size canary 4) retrospective + playbook update for paged-KV. I'll create tasks and assign. :clipboard:

kevin: adding a small follow-up: add a runtime feature flag to cap per-request KV handles as a safety valve. low cost to implement and may prevent similar blowups.

samir: noted. I'll include that in PR. handing off now — monitoring until 23:00 UTC then pass to SRE oncall.

ops-bot: incident marked as mitigated by alex, severity: P2 -> monitoring.

maria: adding final line for CS: mitigation applied (batching rollback + KV bypass), ETA for bugfix: 48h, customers impacted: RJ-498, OakTree Analytics, list of internal tickets: INC-2026-342, RJ-789, PR-6543.

lina: thanks everyone.

samir: bye and will update RFC with root cause once PR lands.
